MDLAreaLight.doc: A light source that illuminates a 3D scene from an area with a specific shape.

MDLAsset.doc: An indexed container for 3D objects and associated information, such as transform hierarchies, meshes, cameras, and lights.

MDLCamera.doc: A point of view for rendering a 3D scene, along with a set of parameters describing an intended appearance for rendering.

MDLCheckerboardTexture.doc: A generator of texel data that creates a checkerboard pattern with two specified colors.

MDLColorSwatchTexture.doc: A generator of texel data that creates a gradient between two specified colors.

MDLLight.doc: The abstract superclass for objects that describe light sources in a scene.

MDLLightProbe.doc: A light source described in terms of the variations in color and intensity of its illumination in all directions.

MDLMaterial.doc: A collection of material properties that together describe the intended surface appearance for rendering a 3D object.

MDLMaterialProperty.doc: A definition for one specific aspect of the rendering parameters for a material.

MDLMesh.doc: A container for vertex buffer data to be used in rendering a 3D object.

MDLMeshBufferData.doc: A memory buffer that stores vertex or index data for a Model I/O mesh.

MDLMeshBufferDataAllocator.doc: A basic allocator implementation that allocates from main memory using data objects.

MDLMeshBufferMap.doc: An object that manages access to a memory buffer used for the data storage of a Model I/O mesh.

MDLMeshBufferZoneDefault.doc: A standard implementation of the MDLMeshBufferZone protocol.

MDLNoiseTexture.doc: A generator of texel data that creates a field of random noise.

MDLNormalMapTexture.doc: A generator of texel data that computes a normal map from a supplied texture.

MDLObject.doc: The base class for objects that are part of a 3D asset, including meshes, cameras, and lights.

MDLObjectContainer.doc: A default implementation for handling object hierarchy relationships in a 3D asset.

MDLPhotometricLight.doc: A light source whose shape, direction, and intensity of illumination are determined by a photometric profile.

MDLPhysicallyPlausibleLight.doc: A light source for use in shading models based on real-world physics.

MDLPhysicallyPlausibleScatteringFunction.doc: A set of material properties that describes a physically realistic shading model for materials.

MDLScatteringFunction.doc: A set of material properties that describes a basic shading model for materials, and the superclass for more complex shading models.

MDLSkyCubeTexture.doc: A generator of texel data that creates cube textures using a physically realistic simulation of the sunlit sky.

MDLStereoscopicCamera.doc: A point of view for rendering a stereoscopic display of a 3D scene.

MDLSubmesh.doc: A container for index buffer data and material information to be used in rendering all or part of a 3D object.

MDLSubmeshTopology.doc: A description of how a submesh’s index buffer data is arranged and how that arrangement should be used to produce the submesh’s intended 3D shape.

MDLTexture.doc: A source of texel data to be used in rendering material surface appearances.

MDLTextureFilter.doc: A description of filtering modes for a renderer to use when sampling from a texture.

MDLTextureSampler.doc: An object that pairs a source of texture data with sampling parameters to be used in rendering the texture.

MDLTransform.doc: A description of the local coordinate space transformations for a 3D object.

MDLURLTexture.doc: A lightweight reference to a URL from which to load texture data.

MDLVertexAttribute.doc: A description of the format of per-vertex data for a single vertex attribute in a mesh object.

MDLVertexAttributeData.doc: An object that provides convenience access to vertex data for a specific vertex attribute of a mesh.

MDLVertexBufferLayout.doc: A MDLVertexBufferLayout object describes layout information for a vertex buffer in a MDLMesh object. A collection of vertex layer objects, vertex attribute objects, and additional information forms a MDLVertexDescriptor object, which completely describes the layout of vertex buffers for a mesh.

MDLVertexDescriptor.doc: A description of the structure, format, and layout for vertex data buffers associated with a mesh.

MDLVoxelArray.doc: A model of a 3D object’s solid volume as a collection of voxels, or cubic units.

MDLComponent.doc: The base protocol for extensible file format support in Model I/O.

MDLLightProbeIrradianceDataSource.doc: Adopt this protocol to provide information for use in automatic placement of light probes around a scene.

MDLMeshBuffer.doc: The general interface for managing storage of vertex and index data used in loading, processing, and rendering meshes.

MDLMeshBufferAllocator.doc: The general interface for managing allocation of data buffers to be used in loading, processing, and rendering meshes.

MDLMeshBufferZone.doc: The general interface for logical pools of memory used in allocation of related mesh data buffers.

MDLNamed.doc: The common interface for Model I/O objects that expose a human-readable name.

MDLObjectContainerComponent.doc: The general interface for classes that can act as containers in an object hierarchy.

MDLTransformComponent.doc: The general interface for classes that manage local coordinate space transforms for 3D objects

MDLCameraProjection.doc: Options for camera projection styles, used by the projection property.

MDLGeometryType.doc: Types of geometric primitives for rendering a submesh, used by the geometryType property.

MDLGeometryTypeLines.doc: Each pair of consecutive indices in the submesh refers to two vertices to be rendered as a line segment.

MDLGeometryTypePoints.doc: Each index in the submesh refers to a vertex to be rendered as a single point.

MDLGeometryTypeQuads.doc: Each set of four consecutive indices in the submesh refers to four vertices to be rendered as a quadrilateral.

MDLGeometryTypeTriangleStrips.doc: The first three consecutive indices in the submesh refer to three vertices to be rendered as a triangle. Each subsequent index refers to another vertex that completes a triangle formed by connecting it to the previous two vertices.

MDLGeometryTypeTriangles.doc: Each set of three consecutive indices in the submesh refers to three vertices to be rendered as a triangle.

MDLGeometryTypeVariableTopology.doc: The submesh’s index buffer does not contain a uniform set of primitives.

MDLIndexBitDepth.doc: Options for the size of integer data in a submesh’s index buffer, used by the indexType property.

MDLIndexBitDepthInvalid.doc: The submesh has not been initialized or its data type is unknown.

MDLIndexBitDepthUInt16.doc: Each index in the submesh’s index buffer is a 16-bit integer.

MDLIndexBitDepthUInt32.doc: Each index in the submesh’s index buffer is a 32-bit integer.

MDLIndexBitDepthUInt8.doc: Each index in the submesh’s index buffer is an 8-bit integer.

MDLLightType.doc: Options for the shape and style of illumination provided by a light, used by the lightType property.

MDLLightTypeAmbient.doc: The light source should illuminate a scene evenly regardless of position or direction.

MDLLightTypeDirectional.doc: The light source illuminates a scene from a uniform direction regardless of its position.

MDLLightTypeDiscArea.doc: The light source illuminates a scene in all directions from an area in the shape of a disc.

MDLLightTypeEnvironment.doc: The illumination from the light is determined by texture images representing a sample of the surrounding environment for a scene.

MDLLightTypeLinear.doc: The light source illuminates a scene in all directions from an area in the shape of a line.

MDLLightTypePhotometric.doc: The illumination from the light is determined by a photometric profile.

MDLLightTypePoint.doc: The light source illuminates a scene in all directions from a specific position.

MDLLightTypeProbe.doc: The illumination from the light is determined by texture images representing a sample of a scene at a specific point.

MDLLightTypeRectangularArea.doc: The light source illuminates a scene in all directions from an area in the shape of a rectangle.

MDLLightTypeSpot.doc: The light source illuminates a scene from a specific position and direction.

MDLLightTypeSuperElliptical.doc: The light source illuminates a scene in all directions from an area in the shape of a superellipse.

MDLLightTypeUnknown.doc: The type of the light is unknown or has not been initialized.

MDLMaterialMipMapFilterMode.doc: Modes for sampling textures at sizes between mipmap levels, used by the mipFilter property.

MDLMaterialMipMapFilterModeLinear.doc: Sampling a texture at a size between mipmap levels should linearly interpolate between mipmap levels.

MDLMaterialMipMapFilterModeNearest.doc: Sampling a texture at a size between mipmap levels should return a texel value from the nearest mipmap level.

MDLMaterialPropertyType.doc: Options for the data type of a material property, used by the type property.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeColor.doc: The material property’s value is a uniform color.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeFloat.doc: The material property’s value is a floating-point scalar.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeFloat2.doc: The material property’s value is a 2-component floating-point vector.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeFloat3.doc: The material property’s value is a 3-component floating-point vector.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeFloat4.doc: The material property’s value is a 4-component floating-point vector.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeMatrix44.doc: The material property’s value is a 4 x 4 floating-point matrix.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeNone.doc: The material property’s value has not been initialized.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeString.doc: The material’s value is a string.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeTexture.doc: The material property’s value is a MDLTextureSampler object that provides both a texture image and texture rendering parameters.

MDLMaterialPropertyTypeURL.doc: The material property’s value is a URL—typically, a URL referencing a texture image.

MDLMaterialSemantic.doc: Options for the semantic use of a material property’s value in rendering a particular surface appearance; used by the semantic property.

MDLMaterialSemanticAmbientOcclusion.doc: The attenuation of ambient light due to local geometry variations on a surface.

MDLMaterialSemanticAmbientOcclusionScale.doc: The scaling factor for ambient occlusion shading.

MDLMaterialSemanticAnisotropic.doc: The degree to which specular highlights elongate in the direction of the local tangent basis.

MDLMaterialSemanticAnisotropicRotation.doc: The angle at which anisotropic effects are rotated relative to the local tangent basis.

MDLMaterialSemanticBaseColor.doc: The inherent color of a surface, to be used as a modulator during shading.

MDLMaterialSemanticBump.doc: The degree of perturbation in a material’s surface.

MDLMaterialSemanticClearcoat.doc: The intensity of a second specular highlight, similar to the gloss that results from a clear coat on an automotive finish.

MDLMaterialSemanticClearcoatGloss.doc: The spread of a second specular highlight, similar to the gloss that results from a clear coat on an automotive finish.

MDLMaterialSemanticDisplacement.doc: The displacement of a material’s surface relative to the surface normal.

MDLMaterialSemanticDisplacementScale.doc: The scaling factor for displacement of a material’s surface.

MDLMaterialSemanticEmission.doc: The color emitted as radiance from a material’s surface.

MDLMaterialSemanticInterfaceIndexOfRefra.doc: The index of refraction for the medium surrounding a material.

MDLMaterialSemanticMaterialIndexOfRefrac.doc: The index of refraction for a material itself.

MDLMaterialSemanticMetallic.doc: The degree to which a material appears as a dielectric surface (lower values) or as a metal (higher values).

MDLMaterialSemanticNone.doc: The material property’s semantic property has not been initialized.

MDLMaterialSemanticObjectSpaceNormal.doc: The variation in the surface normal vectors in a material, relative to model coordinate space.

MDLMaterialSemanticOpacity.doc: The opacity of a material’s surface.

MDLMaterialSemanticRoughness.doc: The degree to which a material appears smooth, affecting both diffuse and specular response.

MDLMaterialSemanticSheen.doc: The intensity of highlights that appear only at glancing angles on a material’s surface.

MDLMaterialSemanticSheenTint.doc: The balance of color for highlights that appear only at glancing angles, between the light color (lower values) and the material’s base color (at higher values).

MDLMaterialSemanticSpecular.doc: The intensity of specular highlights that appear on the material’s surface.

MDLMaterialSemanticSpecularExponent.doc: The exponent to be used in Blinn-Phong approximation of the material’s specular response.

MDLMaterialSemanticSpecularTint.doc: The balance of color for specular highlights, between the light color (lower values) and the material’s base color (at higher values).

MDLMaterialSemanticSubsurface.doc: The degree to which light scatters under the surface of a material.

MDLMaterialSemanticTangentSpaceNormal.doc: The variation in the surface normal vectors in a material, relative to surface tangent coordinate space.

MDLMaterialSemanticUserDefined.doc: The meaning of the material property’s value is not one of the standard semantic uses recognized by Model I/O.

MDLMaterialTextureFilterMode.doc: Modes for sampling textures at coordinates between texels, used by the minFilter and magFilter properties.

MDLMaterialTextureFilterModeLinear.doc: Sampling at texture coordinates between texels should linearly interpolate between texel values.

MDLMaterialTextureFilterModeNearest.doc: Sampling at texture coordinates between texels should return the value of the nearest texel.

MDLMaterialTextureWrapMode.doc: Modes for sampling textures at coordinates outside the texture bounds, used by the sWrapMode, tWrapMode, and rWrapMode properties.

MDLMaterialTextureWrapModeClamp.doc: Sampling at any texture coordinate outside the 0.0 to 1.0 range returns the texel color from the nearest edge.

MDLMaterialTextureWrapModeMirror.doc: Sampling at texture coordinates outside the 0.0 to 1.0 range results in a mirrored tiling effect.

MDLMaterialTextureWrapModeRepeat.doc: Sampling at texture coordinates outside the 0.0 to 1.0 range results in a repeated tiling effect.

MDLMeshBufferType.doc: Options for the content of a mesh buffer, used by the type property and by MDLMeshBufferAllocator methods for creating buffers.

MDLMeshBufferTypeIndex.doc: The buffer contains index data for a MDLSubmesh object.

MDLMeshBufferTypeVertex.doc: The buffer contains per-vertex data for one or more vertex attributes of a MDLMesh object.

MDLProbePlacement.doc: Options affecting automatic placement of light probes in a scene, used with the placeLightProbesWithDensity:heuristic:usingIrradianceDataSource: method.

MDLProbePlacementIrradianceDistribution.doc: An option to examine the lighting conditions at various positions in the scene being evaluated, then place light probes only at the locations where each contributes optimally to scene lighting.

MDLProbePlacementUniformGrid.doc: An option to place light probes at each unit coordinate in a three-dimensional grid that evenly divides the region being evaluated.

MDLTextureChannelEncoding.doc: Options for the data size and type of texel channel values, used by the channelEncoding property.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingFloat16.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 16-bit floating-point value.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingFloat32.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 32-bit floating-point value.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUInt16.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 16-bit unsigned integer.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUInt24.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 24-bit unsigned integer.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUInt32.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 32-bit unsigned integer.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUInt8.doc: Each channel value per texel is an 8-bit unsigned integer.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUint16.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 16-bit unsigned integer.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUint24.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 24-bit unsigned integer.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUint32.doc: Each channel value per texel is a 32-bit unsigned integer.

MDLTextureChannelEncodingUint8.doc: Each channel value per texel is an 8-bit unsigned integer.

MDLVertexFormat.doc: Descriptions of the data size and layout for a vertex attribute, used by the format property.

MDLVertexFormatChar.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatChar2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatChar2Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each with a normalized value of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatChar3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatChar3Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each with a normalized value of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatChar4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatChar4Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each with a normalized value of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatCharBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 8-bit signed integer format.

MDLVertexFormatCharNormalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a normalized scalar of signed 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatCharNormalizedBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 8-bit signed normalized integer format.

MDLVertexFormatFloat.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of 32-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatFloat2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of 32-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatFloat3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of 32-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatFloat4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of 32-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatFloatBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 32-bit floating-point format.

MDLVertexFormatHalf.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of 16-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatHalf2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of 16-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatHalf3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of 16-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatHalf4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of 16-bit floating-point type.

MDLVertexFormatHalfBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 16-bit floating-point format.

MDLVertexFormatInt.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of signed 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatInt1010102Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a packed vector with 4 components of signed integer type. The first three components are 10 bits each, and the fourth component is 2 bits.

MDLVertexFormatInt2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of signed 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatInt3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of signed 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatInt4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of signed 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatIntBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 32-bit signed integer format.

MDLVertexFormatInvalid.doc: The vertex attribute has just been initialized or its format is unknown.

MDLVertexFormatPackedBit.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes in packed vector formats.

MDLVertexFormatShort.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShort2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShort2Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each with a normalized value of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShort3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShort3Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each with a normalized value of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShort4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShort4Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each with a normalized value of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShortBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 16-bit signed integer format.

MDLVertexFormatShortNormalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a normalized scalar of signed 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatShortNormalizedBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 16-bit signed normalized integer format.

MDLVertexFormatUChar.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUChar2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUChar2Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each with a normalized value of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUChar3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUChar3Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each with a normalized value of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUChar4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUChar4Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each with a normalized value of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUCharBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 8-bit unsigned integer format.

MDLVertexFormatUCharNormalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a normalized scalar of unsigned 8-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUCharNormalizedBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 8-bit unsigned normalized integer format.

MDLVertexFormatUInt.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of unsigned 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUInt1010102Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a packed vector with 4 components of unsigned integer type. The first three components are 10 bits each, and the fourth component is 2 bits.

MDLVertexFormatUInt2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of unsigned 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUInt3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of unsigned 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUInt4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of unsigned 32-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUIntBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 32-bit unsigned integer format.

MDLVertexFormatUShort.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a scalar of unsigned 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUShort2.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each of unsigned 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUShort2Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 2 components, each with a normalized value of unsigned 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUShort3.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 3 components, each of unsigned 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUShort4.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each of unsigned 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUShort4Normalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a vector with 4 components, each with a normalized value of unsigned 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUShortBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 16-bit unsigned integer format.

MDLVertexFormatUShortNormalized.doc: The attribute value for each vertex is a normalized scalar of unsigned 16-bit integer type.

MDLVertexFormatUShortNormalizedBits.doc: A bit mask for vertex attributes whose components are in 16-bit unsigned normalized integer format.

MDLAxisAlignedBoundingBox.doc: The minimal volume containing an object, used by the boundingBoxAtTime: method.

MDLVoxelIndexExtent.doc: The corner voxel indices defining a solid rectangular volume of voxels. Used by the voxelIndexExtent property and voxelsWithinExtent: method.

+canExportFileExtension:.doc: Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether the MDLAsset class can write asset data as a file with the specified format extension.

+canImportFileExtension:.doc: Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether the MDLAsset class can read asset data from files with the specified extension.

+placeLightProbesWithDensity:heuristic:u.doc: Automatically creates and places light probes for use in illuminating a scene.

-addObject:.doc: Adds the specified object to the asset’s list of top-level objects.

-boundingBoxAtTime:.doc: Returns the minimum region entirely enclosing the asset’s contents at the specified time sample.

-childObjectsOfClass:.doc: Returns all objects contained in the asset of the specified class.

-exportAssetToURL:.doc: Writes asset data to a file at the specified URL.

-exportAssetToURL:error:.doc: Writes asset data to a file at the specified URL and reports errors that occur during export.

-initWithBufferAllocator:.doc: Initializes an empty asset, using the specified buffer allocator.

-initWithURL:.doc: Initializes an asset from the file at the specified URL.

-initWithURL:vertexDescriptor:bufferAllo.doc: Initializes an asset from the file at the specified URL, using the specified vertex descriptor and buffer allocator.
Initializes an asset from the file at the specified URL, using the specified options for allocating and transforming data during import.

-objectAtIndex:.doc: Returns the top-level object at the specified index in the asset.

-objectAtIndexedSubscript:.doc: Returns the top-level object at the specified index in the asset, using subscript syntax.

-removeObject:.doc: Removes the specified object from the asset’s list of top-level objects.

-bokehKernelWithSize:.doc: Creates and returns a texture, based on the camera’s aperture blade count, to be used in rendering out-of-focus highlights in a scene.

-frameBoundingBox:setNearAndFar:.doc: Moves the camera such that the specified bounding box lies entirely within the camera’s field of view.

-lookAt:.doc: Orients the camera to face toward the specified point.

-lookAt:from:.doc: Sets the camera’s position and orients the camera to face toward the specified point.

-rayTo:forViewPort:.doc: Returns a point, in 3D world coordinates, corresponding to the specified 2D view coordinates.

-initWithDivisions:name:dimensions:chann.doc: Initializes a checkerboard texture with the specified colors and other properties.

-initWithColorGradientFrom:toColor:name:.doc: Initializes a texture that creates a vertical gradient between two colors.

-initWithColorTemperatureGradientFrom:to.doc: Initializes a texture that creates a vertical gradient between two color temperatures.

-irradianceAtPoint:.doc: Returns the radiance of the light as received at a specific point in the same scene.

-irradianceAtPoint:colorSpace:.doc: Returns the radiance of the light as received at a specific point in the same scene, expressed using the specified color space.

+lightProbeWithTextureSize:forLocation:l.doc: Creates a light probe representing the shading environment at a specific point in a scene.

-generateSphericalHarmonicsFromIrradianc.doc: Generates spherical harmonics information based on the light probe’s irradiance texture.

-initWithReflectiveTexture:irradianceTex.doc: Initializes a light probe with the specified cube map textures.

-loadTexturesUsingResolver:.doc: Loads textures using resolver for string paths and NSURLs.

-objectAtIndexedSubscript:.doc: Returns the material property at the specified index in the material, for use with subscript syntax.

-objectForKeyedSubscript:.doc: Returns the material property with the specified name, for use with subscript syntax.

-propertiesWithSemantic:.doc: Returns the complete list of material properties that match the specified material semantic.

-propertyNamed:.doc: Returns the material property with the specified name.

-propertyWithSemantic:.doc: Returns the material property for the specified material semantic.

-removeAllProperties.doc: Removes all material properties from the material.

-removeProperty:.doc: Removes the specified material property from the material.

-resolveTexturesWithResolver:.doc: Resolves all texture string paths as NSURLs with resolver.

-setProperty:.doc: Adds a new material property to or replaces an existing material property in the material.

-initWithName:semantic:.doc: Initializes a material property without a value.

-initWithName:semantic:URL:.doc: Initializes a material property with a URL value.

-initWithName:semantic:color:.doc: Initializes a material property with a color value.

-initWithName:semantic:float2:.doc: Initializes a material property with a 2-component vector value.

-initWithName:semantic:float3:.doc: Initializes a material property with a 3-component vector value.

-initWithName:semantic:float4:.doc: Initializes a material property with a 4-component vector value.

-initWithName:semantic:float:.doc: Initializes a material property with a scalar value.

-initWithName:semantic:matrix4x4:.doc: Initializes a material property with a 4 x 4 matrix value.

-initWithName:semantic:string:.doc: Initializes a material property with a string value.

-initWithName:semantic:textureSampler:.doc: Initializes a material property with a texture sampler object.

-setProperties:.doc: Sets the material property’s attributes to those of the specified material property.

+newBoxWithDimensions:segments:geometryT.doc: Creates a mesh in the shape of a rectangular box or cube.

+newCylinderWithHeight:radii:radialSegme.doc: Generates a mesh in the shape of a right circular or elliptical cylinder.

+newEllipsoidWithRadii:radialSegments:ve.doc: Creates a mesh in the shape of an ellipsoid or sphere.

+newEllipticalConeWithHeight:radii:radia.doc: Generates a mesh in the shape of an elliptical or circular cone.

+newIcosahedronWithRadius:inwardNormals:.doc: Generates a mesh in the shape of a regular 20-sided polyhedron with triangular faces.

+newPlaneWithDimensions:segments:geometr.doc: Generates a mesh in the shape of a rectangular plane.

+newSubdividedMesh:submeshIndex:subdivis.doc: Creates a new mesh by subdividing the specified mesh.

-addAttributeWithName:format:.doc: Adds a vertex attribute to the mesh and creates a new, empty corresponding vertex buffer.

-addNormalsWithAttributeNamed:creaseThre.doc: Generates surface normal data for the mesh based on its vertex position data.

-addTangentBasisForTextureCoordinateAttr.doc: Generates surface tangent data for the mesh based on its vertex position, surface normal, and texture coordinate data.
Generates surface tangent and bitangent data for the mesh based on its vertex position and texture coordinate data.

-generateAmbientOcclusionTextureWithQual.doc: Calculates ambient occlusion (AO) information for the mesh and saves it in the mesh as a material property texture.

-generateAmbientOcclusionTextureWithSize.doc: Calculates ambient occlusion (AO) information for the mesh and saves it in the mesh as a material property texture of the specified size.

-generateAmbientOcclusionVertexColorsWit.doc: Calculates ambient occlusion (AO) information for the mesh and saves it in the mesh as a vertex color attribute.
Calculates ambient occlusion (AO) information for the mesh, using the specified number of rays per sample, and saves it in the mesh as a vertex color attribute.
